note: Follow-up to 0132, measured rather than predicted. After moving Nestor's household root to ~/.nestor this session claimed the downstream face would need NESTOR_HOME set or it would hit the new refusal. Reading rudi193-cmd/homestead showed that was wrong: homestead/keep/nestor_seam.py never calls Nestor's household resolver at all. bind() computes <root>/keep/ledger.jsonl from homestead's own paths.home() and hands set_ledger_path() an explicit value. Verified by running the seam against the changed Nestor in the hostile state ($HOMESTEAD_HOME set, $NESTOR_HOME unset, where nestor.home_paths.home() refuses): bind() pinned /tmp/hh-probe/keep/ledger.jsonl and cascade resolved to it. Its 11 seam invariants pass. The change there was prose only, pushed as claude/nestor-root-rename; the pin stays at v0.2.0 because Nestor's change is unreleased and R14 forbids pinning a branch.

decisions.question: What made a breaking root rename cost the downstream face zero code?
decisions.commitment: A rule the seam wrote down before it had a call site: one resolver on its side of the boundary, never Nestor's.
decisions.why: At Nestor's v0.2.0 pin the two resolvers agreed exactly -- both read $HOMESTEAD_HOME, else <user-home>/.homestead, and both named keep/ledger.jsonl under it. Every incentive pointed at calling Nestor's resolver directly: it was one import, it returned the identical path, and a test asserting the two agreed would have passed. The seam declined, and recorded the agreement as a coincidence it was not going to depend on. That is the whole reason this rename is a prose diff there instead of a silently relocated hash chain -- had bind() leaned on the coincidence, the next pin bump would have moved the ledger out of the household root with nothing raising, which is the exact window bind() exists to close. Worth recording because the discipline looked redundant for as long as it was working, which is when this kind of rule gets deleted.

decisions.question: The session predicted the seam would break. It did not. What does that cost?
decisions.commitment: Record the wrong prediction alongside the measurement, and correct it to the user in the same breath rather than quietly shipping the right answer.
decisions.why: The prediction was made from Nestor's side without reading the consumer, on the reasonable-sounding assumption that a face named homestead would use the resolver named homestead_paths. It was stated to the user as a required follow-up. A blast-radius claim about a downstream repo is exactly the kind that is cheap to assert and expensive to be wrong about in either direction -- overstating it invites a change nobody needed, in a seam whose own header says do not propose changes to Nestor from here. The general form: an integration claim is not derived until the consumer has been read, and preferably run.

decisions.question: Bump the pin so the face is on the renamed module?
decisions.commitment: No. It stays at v0.2.0, and what changes at the bump is documented instead.
decisions.why: Nestor's rename is unreleased -- it is a branch with no tag, and fleet rule R14 forbids pinning anything that ships to a branch. Bumping would also be a change nobody needs: the seam imports neither nestor.homestead_paths nor nestor.home_paths, so the rename is invisible to it. What the next bumper actually needs is the two facts they cannot see from the diff -- the module is renamed, and Nestor now refuses to resolve when $HOMESTEAD_HOME is set without $NESTOR_HOME -- plus the note that the refusal is reachable only through the resolver this seam does not call. Those are now in PRECONDITION 1.
